definition: Critic-free policy optimization for language models: for each prompt the policy samples a group of completions, each completion's advantage is its reward normalised by the group's mean and standard deviation, and the update is a clipped surrogate usually with a KL penalty to a reference policy -- so the baseline comes from the group rather than from a learned value network, which is the property nearly every source cites as its reason for choosing it. Across these sources it functions less as a fixed algorithm than as a substrate everything else is bolted onto: dense per-step rewards replacing the sequence-level one, advantages shifted by a detached teacher-student log-probability gap, credit redistributed by how rare a solution form is, updates restricted to a token subset, and rewards supplied by rubrics regenerated from the model's own rollouts, by an LLM judge, by a verifier, or by SQL executed against a source table. The sources agree on its characteristic failure and disagree about the fix: policy entropy collapses as reward rises, along a curve one paper fits as R = -a*exp(H) + b, with the driver identified variously as the covariance between token probability and advantage, as an imbalance between tokens whose updates lower entropy and those that raise it, and as the behaviour of positive-advantage tokens specifically -- while a theoretical comparison argues an entropy bonus buys control only by permanently moving the stationary point, where covariance-targeted control reaches the unregularized optimum once annealed. Three structural criticisms of the group-relative estimator recur: it produces exactly zero advantage whenever every rollout in a group agrees, wasting the rollouts; its per-completion uniformity is frequency-skewed once credit is aggregated by solution structure, so a recurring correct form accumulates positive coefficient mass in proportion to how often it is sampled; and its standard-deviation and length normalisations introduce optimization biases that a named variant removes. Two further sources bound what it achieves rather than how it runs, and they disagree: measured by pass@k at large k, RLVR-trained models lose to their own base models, which reads as sharpening the sampling distribution rather than adding capability -- but scoring the chain as well as the final answer reverses that verdict at every k, on the grounds that base models win by producing wrong chains that land on right answers. One source adds a consequence outside the training loop entirely: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals benchmark-contamination detectors rely on, with PPO-style importance sampling and clipping identified as the cause.

evidence.note: Gives each retrieval step of a search agent a dense reward built from two ground-truth-conditioned signals — how much the step raised the model's likelihood of the correct answer, and how necessary the step looks in hindsight — and fuses them asymmetrically so that a step which helps locally but is redundant globally is discounted.
evidence.title: BiCAA: Bidirectional Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Agent

evidence.note: Re-scores a search agent's own sampled tokens under a teacher that has been shown the instance's supporting evidence, and uses the detached teacher-student gap to nudge the GRPO advantage up or down on search and answer tokens only, without adding a distillation loss or changing anything at inference.
evidence.title: EviSD: Evidence-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Agents

evidence.note: Estimates what a continuous latent thought is worth by freezing the context after it and averaging the rewards of several answers sampled from that fixed context, then credits latent positions with the resulting thought-level advantage and answer positions with the ordinary group-relative one.
evidence.title: Latent Thought Credit: Multi-Answer Credit Assignment for Latent Reasoning

evidence.note: Inserts a stage before RL in which the model extracts textual lessons from its own successful and failed rollouts, filters them by measured marginal utility on a held-out probe set, and distills the surviving pool into its own weights — so that GRPO starts from a policy that fails all-eight-samples less often.
evidence.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution

evidence.note: Treats a policy's per-problem failure probability as a random variable over the problem distribution and shows that REINFORCE, pass@K training and MaxRL each optimize a single moment of it, then proposes minimizing the first T moments jointly — which is exactly minimizing the expected truncated number of rollouts needed to reach a first success.
evidence.title: Beyond the Mean: Multi-Moment Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Replaces PPO's scalar mean-squared-error critic head with a categorical predictor over a discretized value support trained by cross-entropy against Gaussian-smoothed targets, decodes it back to a scalar for an unchanged GAE update, and shows the resulting critic is better calibrated and produces near-symmetric advantages where the MSE critic penalizes failures two-to-three times harder than it rewards successes.
evidence.title: Start Classifying: Categorical Critics for LLM Reinforcement Learning

evidence.note: Supervises audio reasoning with per-question rubrics generated from the raw waveform, and keeps the signal alive as the policy improves by regenerating the rubrics from the model's own rollouts each step and pruning any criterion that every rollout satisfies or none does.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics as Rewards for Audio Reasoning

evidence.note: Scores each reasoning step of a translation by how much appending it raises a frozen reference model's teacher-forced likelihood of the gold translation, and adds that as a dense per-step reward on top of sequence-level quality — after first establishing that explicit reasoning helps long and hard inputs while drifting on terminology and style.
evidence.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation

evidence.note: Diagnoses label-free RLVR's collapse as a shortcut in which the same answer-level consensus signal both estimates the reward and receives the gradient, and fixes it by masking the answer span from updates entirely — so a reward can only be raised by improving the reasoning that produces the answer.
evidence.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR

evidence.note: Recasts long-document visual question answering as building an explicit evidence graph whose nodes are grounded document blocks and whose edges are reasoning dependencies, and verifies the graph causally — masking the evidence it cites flips 82.8% of correct answers while masking uncited evidence changes 9.6%.
evidence.title: DocTrace: Towards Traceable Long Document VQA via Hierarchical Evidence Graph Reasoning

evidence.note: Shows that GRPO's per-completion uniformity is frequency-skewed once credit is aggregated by solution structure — a recurring correct form accumulates positive coefficient mass proportional to how often it is sampled — and rebalances it by a rarity exponent over a partition built from deterministic cue signatures rather than a judge model.
evidence.title: When Correct Solutions Repeat: Rarity-Aware Credit Redistribution for GRPO

evidence.note: Splits a video model's latent computation into perception latents that always ground the question in visual evidence and reasoning latents allocated only when the question needs inference, and shows that reasoning latents without rationale supervision are worse than no reasoning latents at all.
evidence.title: Perception Before Reasoning: Dynamic Latent Reasoning for Video Understanding and Question Answering

evidence.note: A GRPO variant that teaches multimodal models to refuse when a referred object is absent, without losing localization accuracy on cases where it is present.
evidence.title: Teaching MLLMs to Say No: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension via Refusal Calibrated GRPO

evidence.note: A speculative-decoding rollout engine for RL post-training that keeps the target sampling distribution exact while adapting the drafter at two timescales.
evidence.title: SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts

evidence.note: A GRPO variant for flow-based generative models that replaces SDE training rollouts with an ODE step plus a Langevin correction, aligning training samples with the deterministic sampler used at test time.
evidence.title: LC-GRPO: Bridging Train-Inference Gap for Flow-Based GRPO with Langevin Correction

evidence.note: Turns token-level teacher-student log-probability gaps into turn-level credit for agentic RL by recursively updating a Bayesian belief in log-odds space, identifying pivotal turns without a critic.
evidence.title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

evidence.note: Trains a multimodal agent to orchestrate twelve video-analysis tools for anomaly detection with GRPO under a dual reward that combines exact-match rule checks with an LLM judge scoring logicality, relevance and completeness, and releases the benchmark it is evaluated on.
evidence.title: VTO: Visual Tool Orchestration for Video Anomaly Detection

evidence.note: Builds a dense process reward without a learned verifier or an online judge, by aligning generated reasoning steps to the process-labelled reference steps that existing datasets already contain using numerical, symbolic and lexical matching rules, gated so a partial reference match cannot override a wrong final answer.
evidence.title: StructReward: Efficient Structured Process Rewards for Self-Correcting Multimodal Reasoning

evidence.note: Replaces the single tolerance threshold that RLVR uses to score floating-point answers with a hybrid reward pairing a hard clinical-safety constraint against a continuous precision-sensitive term, and adds a reward for stating the computational formula explicitly so an external verifier can check it.
evidence.title: MedCalc-R1: Knowledge-Guided Reward Framework for Medical Mathematical Reasoning

evidence.note: Uses chain-of-thought about required capabilities as training-time supervision for a skill retriever -- distilled from a teacher in stage one and refined by retrieval-rewarded GRPO in stage two -- so that at inference the model encodes the bare query with no generation at all.
evidence.title: SkillReason: Reasoning-Enhanced Agent Skill Retrieval for Implicit User Requests

evidence.note: Gives the teacher in on-policy self-distillation access to each completed student rollout and its verified outcome, adapting it to preserve behaviour on successes and redirect failures toward verified success, while the student keeps a prefix-only interface it can actually deploy.
evidence.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation

evidence.note: Shows on four internal Netflix verification tasks that explicit reasoning usually degrades subjective judgement, that applying RLVR to fix it makes the policy abandon deliberation for short heuristic guessing, and that a length bonus gated on answer correctness is what stops the collapse.
evidence.title: LLM Reasoning for Subjective Tasks: Failure Modes, Mitigation, and Dynamic Reasoning Routing

evidence.note: Separates how well a policy currently does on a task from how positively that task responds to further training, shows the second is reproducible across independent runs and predicts downstream value at matched current pass rate, and estimates it from a short probe run before RL begins.
evidence.title: Beyond Solvability: Task Learnability as a Static Prior for LLM RL Post-Training

evidence.note: Explores in weight space rather than token space during RLVR by sampling policies from a variational posterior at rollout time, and introduces a training-time exploration metric -- how often a method produces a correct rollout on a prompt where GRPO produced none -- because entropy and pass@k cannot tell exploration from degeneration.
evidence.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning

evidence.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
evidence.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

evidence.note: Points out that the group-relative policy gradient is a second-order U-statistic over pairs of rollouts rather than a sum of independent per-rollout contributions, and reallocates rollout compute accordingly -- treating prefixes as vertices and pair-gradient terms as edges, then correcting the resulting selection bias by inverse joint-inclusion weighting.
evidence.title: PAIR: Pairwise-Aware Inclusion Reweighting for Adaptive Rollout Allocation in RLVR

evidence.note: Trains an open-weight model with GRPO against a safety-gated LLM-as-a-judge rubric for financial advice, then audits the result with a judge-independent causal estimator on logged outcomes -- and finds the two evaluations rank the other systems differently, with the untrained base model last on the rubric and second on the audit.
evidence.title: GRPO for Financial Advice Generation: Outperforming Commercial LLMs under CATE Evaluation

evidence.note: Gives a search agent an explicitly reversible trajectory tree with reflect and backtrack as first-class actions, and trains the reflection policy with a dense local signal distilled from a teacher that can see the whole trajectory alongside the sparse terminal reward the local decision is ultimately judged by.
evidence.title: LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation

evidence.note: Splits a spatial-reasoning chain of thought into explicitly typed segments -- perception, including depth, and reasoning -- and gives each its own process reward and its own advantage term, so that the two do not compete for credit under a single outcome signal.
evidence.title: SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward

evidence.note: Identifies double-checking after the correct answer is already derived as 'invalid thinking', and trains a GRPO variant with a compress reward that targets exactly that portion.
evidence.title: Optimizing Length Compression in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Addresses wasted rollouts in critic-free RL on prompts where every sampled rollout is already correct and the advantage estimate is therefore zero.
evidence.title: Miner: Mining Intrinsic Mastery for Data-Efficient RL in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Uses elliptical bonuses over a language model's own hidden-state representations as a diversity signal, validates it in a clean inference-time selection setting, then transfers the same signal into RL post-training — where it eliminates the diversity collapse that degrades pass@k at large k.
evidence.title: Representation-Based Exploration for Language Models: From Test-Time to Post-Training

evidence.note: Argues that Shannon entropy is the wrong criterion for picking which tokens to train on in RLVR, and selects tokens instead by the Jensen-Shannon divergence of their logit distribution from the group average, updating only the top 10% of these 'unique' tokens.
evidence.title: Beyond Entropy: Learning from Token-Level Distributional Deviations for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Shows that benchmark contamination in reasoning models is alarmingly easy to hide: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals contamination detectors rely on, and PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the cause — implying a broad class of RL methods conceals contamination inherently.
evidence.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Establishes that RL trades policy entropy for reward along a predictable exponential curve R = -a·exp(H) + b, derives that entropy change is driven by the covariance between action probability and advantage, and controls it by restricting updates to the highest-covariance tokens.
evidence.title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

evidence.note: Trains reasoning models to be concise in proportion to difficulty by modulating the token penalty and the target length per problem, and fixes a distortion that naive reward weighting introduces into group-normalized RL.
evidence.title: The Overthinker's DIET: Cutting Token Calories with DIfficulty-AwarE Training

evidence.note: Shows that the roughly 20% of CoT tokens with the highest entropy act as decision forks, and that restricting RLVR policy-gradient updates to only those tokens matches or beats full-gradient training, with the advantage growing with model size.
evidence.title: Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Reduces the question of whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token, shows that under GRPO what matters is that scalar's deviation from a policy-weighted baseline rather than its own value, and proves the deviation averages to zero over a batch.
evidence.title: On the Entropy Dynamics in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

evidence.note: TRACED scores a reasoning chain by the geometry of its hidden-state trajectory -- net displacement as progress and curvature as stability -- and uses the two as features for a Gaussian classifier that separates correct from incorrect chains without reading the text.
evidence.title: Beyond Scalars: Evaluating and Understanding LLM Reasoning via Geometric Progress and Stability

evidence.note: Recasts entropy collapse as an imbalance of 'entropy flow' — tokens whose update lowers entropy persistently outweigh those that raise it — and rebalances the two sets with a closed-form coefficient computed from each batch, without reference policies or entropy bonuses.
evidence.title: Understanding and Preventing Entropy Collapse in RLVR with On-Policy Entropy Flow Optimization

evidence.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
evidence.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

evidence.note: A systematic empirical study of entropy in RLVR that finds entropy correlates with response diversity but only weakly and inconsistently with accuracy, identifies clipping thresholds, off-policy updates and data diversity as its drivers, and argues positive-advantage tokens are what collapses it.
evidence.title: Revisiting Entropy in Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Turns a linear chain of thought into a dependency DAG, labels each node as advancing the frontier or reviewing it, and prunes review nodes on two graph criteria — too few descendants, or too late in the trace — cutting 42% of tokens while accuracy holds or rises.
evidence.title: Graph-Based Chain-of-Thought Pruning for Reducing Redundant Reflections in Reasoning LLMs

evidence.note: A position paper arguing that reading a reasoning model's intermediate tokens as 'reasoning' or 'thinking' is unsupported by the available evidence and actively harmful, and collating experiments in which trace semantics and solution accuracy come apart.
evidence.title: Position: Stop Anthropomorphizing Intermediate Tokens as Reasoning/Thinking Traces!

evidence.note: Introduces EDIS, a trajectory-level score that measures how unstably token entropy evolves during generation, and uses it to select better reasoning rollouts at inference and to curate training samples in RL.
evidence.title: EDIS: Diagnosing LLM Reasoning via Entropy Dynamics

evidence.note: Reads a reasoning trajectory as a multi-step pseudo-gradient descent on the model's own parameters, which makes each token an optimization step, the trajectory an inner loop, and the training regime a meta-learning problem in which the question is the task.
evidence.title: Deciphering Trajectory-Aided LLM Reasoning: An Optimization Perspective

evidence.note: Proves that an entropy bonus permanently moves the stationary point of RL training while covariance-targeted control reaches the unregularized optimum once its coefficient is annealed, and that the bonus shrinks the stability margin where the targeted methods leave it intact.
evidence.title: A Comparative Theoretical Analysis of Entropy Control Methods in Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

evidence.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

name: GRPO
